“In the Garden of Eden Adam saw the animals before he named…” — Alfred North Whitehead (The Aims of Education)

Verified English quotation. Primary source: The Aims of Education. Theme: education.

Source and attribution

The archive attributes this English wording to The Aims of Education and files it under Process Philosophy. That locator distinguishes the passage from loose internet attributions: readers can return to the named work or section to check translation, surrounding argument, and edition-specific wording.

About Alfred North Whitehead

Alfred North Whitehead (1861–1947) was an English mathematician-philosopher who co-authored Principia Mathematica with Russell, then developed process metaphysics at Harvard. Science and the Modern World and Process and Reality rethink nature as events, not inert stuff.

How to read this passage

Across 4 recurring voices here (notably Mary Wollstonecraft and Plato), education is framed through Platonism and Renaissance Humanism. Some passages define education; others warn how it fails; still others relocate it inside habit, community, or language. This passage enters that discussion through education, experience.

Concepts in this quote

Education
Education appears in this archive as a live philosophical concern—not a slogan. These verified English passages show how thinkers treat education as a problem of judgment, practice, or explanation.
Experience
Experience is the lived encounter with world and self—foundation or limit for knowledge, art, and ethics.
